context:
Goal: a test's verdict never depends on how fast the machine is.
Problem (rule): decision test-practices P5 bans every wall-clock wait in a test. PR #1177 rewrites P5 to allow a "hang guard": a wait limit that only stops a test that hangs. It cites only a plan line, not your ruling. A reviewer showed that a speed limit can pass as a hang guard just by its label.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/test-practices.md P5 on main; docs/plans/time-pinned-tests.md; 252 existing wait limits in tests.
Departs from: main's P5, which bans every wall-clock wait — a and b allow a hang-guard limit.
Meanwhile lane cs-revive-unfinished ships #1177's finder fix and leaves P5's text alone.

options.label: Allow hang guards as written
options.lose: A speed limit can hide as a hang guard.

options.gain: Real hang guards stay, and speed limits get caught: each limit must be several times the measured run, with the figure beside it, as CI job limits already require.
options.label: Allow them with a size rule (recommended)
Keep P5 as it is, and ship only #1177's finder fix
options.lose: The 252 limits stay against P5's text.

short: Test hang guards: allow, allow with a size rule, or keep the ban
title: May a test keep a wait limit that only stops a hung test (a hang guard)?
why: PR #1177 changes your test rule without your ruling, so only you can say yes or no.
